sections.section_title: The Ministry Received and the Conduct It Demands
sections.summary: Paul declares he does not lose heart because the new covenant ministry was received by God's mercy, and he has renounced disgraceful underhanded ways, refusing to practice cunning or tamper with God's word, commending himself instead by the open statement of truth to every person's conscience in the sight of God.

sections.section_title: The Veiled Gospel and the God of This Age
sections.summary: Paul argues that when his gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing, whose minds the god of this age has blinded to prevent them from seeing the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

sections.section_title: What Is Proclaimed and What Has Shone
sections.summary: Paul proclaims not himself but Christ Jesus as Lord, identifying himself as the Corinthians' servant for Jesus' sake, and describes God's illumination of hearts as a new-creation act parallel to the original creation of light from darkness in Genesis 1:3, giving the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

sections.section_title: The Thesis -- Treasure in Clay Vessels
sections.summary: Paul states that the treasure of the gospel is held in fragile clay vessels (ostrakina skeue) by divine design, so that the surpassing power (hyperbole tes dynameos) is unmistakably God's and not the apostle's.

sections.section_title: The Catalogue of Afflictions -- Pressed but Not Crushed
sections.summary: Paul catalogues four paired afflictions -- afflicted but not crushed, perplexed but not despairing, persecuted but not forsaken, struck down but not destroyed -- illustrating the clay-vessel thesis that divine power sustains the apostle at the edge of destruction without allowing the final step.

sections.section_title: Carrying the Death of Jesus -- The Logic of the Cross in the Apostle's Body
sections.summary: Paul describes always carrying the dying (nekrosis) of Jesus in his body so that the life (zoe) of Jesus is manifested in the same body, arguing that the apostle is always being given over to death for Jesus' sake so that death works in the apostle but life flows to the community.

sections.section_title: The Spirit of Faith, Resurrection, and the Community's Benefit
sections.summary: Grounded in the psalmist's faith under affliction (Psalm 116:10), Paul proclaims because he believes, knowing that God who raised Jesus will raise him also and present him together with the Corinthians, with everything done for their sake so that expanding grace produces expanding thanksgiving to God's glory.

sections.section_title: The Inner Renewal and the Weight of Glory
sections.summary: Paul repeats that he does not lose heart: though the outer person wastes away the inner person is renewed daily, present affliction is light and momentary compared to the eternal weight of glory it prepares, and the apostle's gaze is fixed on unseen eternal realities rather than on the seen and transient.
